findings.claim: Present-tense corpus counts in descriptive docs went stale with the new fixture directory and are not marked.
findings.evidence: docs/analysis-report.md:547-549 says 'the 41 dev-corpus fixtures in evals/fixtures/ … evals/fixtures/ holds 42 directories (41 filings + repo_hygiene)'; ADR-021 §b8 (specs/decisions/ADR-021-benchmark-instrument.md:171-178) says 'Forty-two fixture directories are committed'. At HEAD iter_fixtures yields 42 and ls -d evals/fixtures/*/ gives 43. ADR-030 §g notes the bench artifact predates the fixture but these sentences carry no dated marker.
findings.repro: python3 -c 'from evals.oracle import iter_fixtures; print(len(list(iter_fixtures())))' → 42; ls -d evals/fixtures/*/ | wc -l → 43; sed -n 547,549p docs/analysis-report.md
findings.acceptance: Either a dated parenthetical at both spots ('42 filings / 43 directories since ADR-030; bench artifact of record is n=41') or the wording re-scoped to the artifact's population rather than the present tree.

findings.claim: prompts/017 mis-attributes the 7.4 ratio to a legitimate filing; it is jpm-2024's last-span defect.
findings.evidence: prompts/017-d3-non-last-span-dominance.md:29-31: 'the ratio is 5.15 on the one defective fixture and 5.6–7.4 on legitimate pointer-heavy filings (wfc-2008, cvx-2015, mrk-1995)'. Re-measured: wfc 6.95, cvx 5.76, mrk 5.58 (legit range 5.58–6.95); 7.41 is jpm-2024 (last_item_dominates, ambiguous), which ADR-030 §b2 correctly lists as a defect.
findings.repro: largest/second-largest extracted span ratio per fixture at origin/main; compare ADR-030 §b2 list vs prompts/017 line 30
findings.acceptance: prompts/017 reads '5.6–7.0 on legitimate pointer-heavy filings (wfc-2008, cvx-2015, mrk-1995); the two last-span defects read 7.41/4.99', matching ADR-030 §b2.

findings.claim: ADR-030 §c reason 2 uses the held-out outcome as evidence for the escalation ruling while §g disclaims any held-out derivation; under the held-out README's burn rule (influence, not re-running) and the axp-2008 precedent, the two statements conflict.
findings.evidence: specs/decisions/ADR-030-non-last-span-dominance.md §c.2: 'At 0.55 no committed real filing, dev or held-out, fires (§b1 / §b1-held-out)' given as the second of three reasons; §g: 'any threshold chosen on held-out data (the held-out table enters no derivation…)'; §b1-held-out commits doc_status + largest-span item/fraction for all 5 held-out fixtures. evals/heldout/README.md:20-22 burn rule; :174-181 axp-2008 precedent.
findings.acceptance: Either §c.2 cites only the 26 dev real filings (the dev FP set alone carries the argument; the held-out table stays a read-only report) or the ADR/README record that the policy ruling consulted the five held-out outcomes and says why that is not a burn under the rule's own text.
